works.title: Learning the Path to Ion Separation: A Proof-of-Concept for Machine Learning-Assisted Inverse Design (MLAID) of Nanofiltration Membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Advancing the design of polymeric membranes through material screening and discovery offers a powerful strategy to guide future membrane fabrication tailored to a wide range of separation challenges. Traditional trial-and-error methods often fall short in navigating this large monomer and process-design space, whereas machine learning-assisted inverse design (MLAID) can provide an extensible workflow for translating literature-derived membrane knowledge into ranked experimental candidates. Building on prior inverse-design strategies that combine machine learning (ML) with Bayesian optimization (BO), this study applies MLAID to prioritize membrane candidates within a target-defined nanofiltration (NF) design space. MLAID models are trained with membrane fabrication data, and their underlying patterns are interpreted through Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). SHAP was used to investigate model-attribution patterns, and BO was used to prioritize monomer and fabrication-condition combinations for producing polyamide membranes with targeted permeability and selectivity. The MLAID framework prioritized candidate formulations across target salt-water permeabilities of 4 to 12 LMH/bar (L m–2 h–1 bar–1), with Na2SO4 rejection used as the experimental benchmark. Fabrication and testing served as the experimental decision gate for evaluating the model-prioritized candidates. Overall, this study demonstrates how ML/BO-guided prioritization can accelerate identification of promising monomers and fabrication conditions within an encoded design space, while providing a workflow backbone that can expand as richer target-specific data sets, descriptors, and validation become available.

works.title: Building Highly Efficient Nanofiltration Membrane with Enhanced Porosity via Incorporating Chitosan-Based Derivatives
institutions: Hunan University of Science and Technology
Hunan University of Science and Technology , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Thin-film composite (TFC) nanofiltration membranes are widely employed for water treatment due to their effective retention of multivalent ions and organic contaminants. However, a significant challenge persists, with increased water permeability often compromising selectivity and structure stability. Here, we present the design and synthesis of highly efficient TFC membranes through the incorporation of water-soluble chitosan derivatives (carboxymethyl chitosan, CMCS, and arginine-modified chitosan, CSR) as a third component in the aqueous phase during interfacial polymerization. The chitosan derivatives, enriched with abundant active groups and strong charge properties, served as both additives and amino comonomers, optimizing the pore structure of the polyamide separation layer. The optimized CMCS/PIP-TFC membrane achieves a pure water permeance of 15.6 LMH/bar while maintaining &gt;95% Na2SO4 rejection and exhibits a flux recovery rate &gt; 99% after bovine serum albumin fouling. Molecular simulations reveal that the incorporated chitosan chains increase the fractional free volume from 14.3 to 29.9%. Additionally, the unique charge properties of chitosan endow the TFC membrane with remarkable antibacterial properties. This study provides new insights and strategies for the development of high-performance TFC membranes for industrial applications.

works.title: Solid-vapor interface confined repair for pH-resistant nanofiltration membranes with high performance in lithium-ion battery recycling
works.abstract: Nanofiltration (NF) application in recovering valuable metals from spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is limited by the poor acid resistance and inadequate selectivity of conventional polyamide membranes. Triazine-based polyamine networks inherently possess superior pH stability and positive surface charges favorable for multivalent cation rejection, yet their synthesis is hampered by the low reactivity of cyanuric chloride (CC), resulting in loosely cross-linked active layers with suboptimal separation performance. Here, we introduce a solid-vapor interface confined repair (SVICR) strategy that transforms a preformed loose triazine-polyamine network into a dense, defect-free separation layer through spatially confined post-repair with diethylenetriamine vapor. This interface-limiting process efficiently consumes residual chlorine sites while minimizing thickness increase and hydraulic resistance. The resulting membranes exhibit exceptional mono−/multivalent ion selectivity in 2 M H₂SO₄, with separation factors of 53, 40, and 55 for Li + /Co 2+ , Li + /Ni 2+ , and Li + /Mn 2+ , respectively, alongside a water permeance of 4–8 L·m −2 ·h −1 ·bar −1 . Moreover, the membranes demonstrate outstanding long-term stability under extreme conditions, sustaining less than 2% performance decline after 21 days of exposure to 2 M H₂SO₄, 2 M HCl, or 1 M NaOH. The SVICR strategy establishes a processable and effective platform for fabricating pH-resistant NF membranes, advancing sustainable LIB recycling technologies.

works.title: Missing Evidence in Interfacial Polymerization: Challenges and Opportunities for In Situ Observation of Polyamide Membrane Formation
works.abstract: Abstract Polyamide (PA) thin-film composite membranes are the dominant platform for reverse osmosis and nanofiltration. However, despite decades of development, the dynamic formation process of PA layers during interfacial polymerization (IP) remains insufficiently understood. Existing mechanistic interpretations are largely based on retrospective relationship analyses of formed membrane nanostructure with certain IP reaction conditions rather than direct in situ observation of transient interfacial events. The ultrafast kinetics, nanoscale reaction zone, liquid–liquid interfacial environment, and highly nonequilibrium nature of IP make the in situ observation challenging. Herein, we critically examine the major mechanistic interpretations for the nanostructure formation of fully and semiaromatic PA, including convections, interfacial degassing, monomer eruption, reaction-diffusion, and water templating. Inconsistencies and limitations of these interpretations are briefly discussed, further driving the introduction of the progress and limitations of existing in situ IP observation techniques. Despite these techniques enabling in situ spatial or temporal characterization of PA formation during IP, they still lack high-resolution spatiotemporal monitoring and excellent compatibility with the susceptible liquid–liquid interface. To address these challenges, we further envision the next-generation in situ IP observation platform combining miniaturized IP reactors, controllable reaction initiation, and ultrafast vitrification function as inspired by the advanced time-resolved cryogenic electron microscopy in biological studies. This platform is expected to allow direct in situ characterization of the transient IP reaction stages, thereby improving the fundamental understanding of the rapid and dynamic formation of diverse PA nanostructures and thus guiding the rational design of high-performance PA membranes.

works.title: Powder-to-membrane transformation affording 2D/3D COF membranes for molecular separations
works.abstract: The rapid advancement of reticular chemistry has enabled the synthesis of thousands of covalent organic framework (COF) powders bearing various structures and functions. Nevertheless, processing these COF powders into application-ready membranes with precise separation capacity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a dynamic covalent chemistry-based dual-drive strategy is harnessed to drive macroscopic structural variation, achieving the transformation of powdered COFs into defect-free COF membranes. This powder-to-membrane transformation is enabled by the internal factor of framework reconstruction and the external driving force of acid attack, showcasing high processibility, which affords scalable two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) COF membranes with a maximum area of 225 cm2. The optimum TpPa membrane demonstrates excellent performance in molecular sieving, displaying high rejections towards dye (99%) and pharmaceutical molecules (98%) and a pure water permeance of 179.0 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. Moreover, our dual-drive transformation outperforms conventional methods in fabrication efficiency, conversion ratio, separation performance, etc., offering a green, efficient, versatile, and scalable strategy for the preparation and application of COF membranes in chemical engineering separations. Processing covalent organic framework (COF) powders into application-ready membranes with precise separation capacity remains challenging. Here, the authors demonstrate a dual-drive strategy that drives macroscopic structural variation and transforms COF powders into defect-free membranes.

works.title: Highly Efficient Removal of Chlorophenolic Disinfection Byproducts from Water by PMMA/PEG Asymmetric Blend Membranes
works.abstract: The widespread use of disinfectants has led to the generation of large amounts of harmful organic disinfection byproducts (DBPs), posing a serious threat to human health. Membrane separation technology has been extensively applied for the removal of organic pollutants from water. However, conventional nanofiltration membranes often suffer from low rejection efficiency for small neutral organic molecules due to size exclusion and charge repulsion limitations. Reverse osmosis membranes achieve higher rejection but are hindered by high energy consumption. In this work, we fabricated a series of poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)/polyethylene glycol (PEG) blend membranes with different blending ratios via a simple non-solvent induced phase separation method, and systematically characterized their structure and performance. Among them, the membrane with a PMMA/PEG ratio of 8:2 exhibited an asymmetric structure featuring a dense top layer and a porous sublayer. Compared with other blend ratios, this membrane showed the best rejection performance toward four neutral chlorophenol DBPs with molecular weights ≤ 200 Da. Notably, the rejection of 2,4-dichlorophenol reached as high as 91.71%. The design and fabrication of this blend nanofiltration membrane material offers a straightforward and efficient material platform for the removal of chlorophenol DBPs from water environments.

works.title: Advanced nanocomposite membranes for sustainable water reuse in agriculture
works.journal: Frontiers in Membrane Science and Technology
works.abstract: Agricultural irrigation accounts for the large majority of global freshwater withdrawals, and mounting water scarcity is driving increased interest in reusing municipal, industrial, and agricultural wastewater as an irrigation source. Membrane-based treatment spanning microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, reverse osmosis, forward osmosis, membrane bioreactors, and membrane distillation already underpins much of this reuse, but conventional membranes remain constrained by fouling, high energy demand, and an inherent trade-off between removing contaminants and retaining agronomically valuable nutrients. This review examines nanocomposite membranes as a materials-based strategy for overcoming these limitations. It surveys the classification of nanomaterials used in membrane design (zero-to three-dimensional fillers, including metal/metal oxide nanoparticles, carbon nanotubes, graphene oxide, and metal-organic frameworks, as well as emerging bio-based alternatives) and the principal fabrication routes dope blending, interfacial polymerization, surface coating, electrospinning, and in situ growth used to integrate them into polymeric and ceramic matrices. Evidence from the literature is synthesized across key performance dimensions relevant to agricultural reuse: water permeability and flux, fouling resistance and antimicrobial activity, selectivity and contaminant rejection, and mechanical, thermal, and chemical stability, with particular attention to configurations such as photocatalytic and antimicrobial nanofiltration membranes and fertilizer-drawn forward osmosis systems that target nutrient-selective performance. The review finds that nanocomposite modification can produce substantial, mechanism-specific improvements over pristine membranes, but that translating these laboratory-scale gains into field-scale agricultural practice will depend on resolving open questions around nanoparticle leaching and environmental safety, manufacturing scalability, and cost. Emerging directions, including machine-learning-guided membrane design, hybrid process integration, and green-synthesized nanomaterials, are identified as promising routes toward more sustainable, field-ready nanocomposite membrane technologies for agricultural water reuse.

works.title: N-Heterocyclic Organobase-Mediated Interfacial Polymerization for the Rapid Synthesis of Highly Crystalline COF Membranes
institutions: Hangzhou Self-Healing Materials Technology Co., Ltd. , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal candidates for constructing high-performance molecular separation membranes. Interfacial polymerization (IP) represents an important approach for fabricating continuous COF membranes. This study presents an N-heterocyclic organobase-mediated IP (N-het-IP) strategy to rapidly fabricate highly crystalline, continuous COF membranes at the interface. The key of the N-het-IP strategy lies in the presynthesized aqueous-phase tertiary amine intermediates derived from the N-heterocyclic organobase (such as piperazine) and aldehyde monomers (such as Tp). The tertiary amine intermediates with a Tp core and N-heterocyclic segments take part in the dynamic amine exchange reaction with organic-phase amine monomers, inducing interfacial membrane formation and COF crystalline transformation within 30 min under mild conditions. Simultaneously, the interfacial assembly of the tertiary amine intermediates constructs an amphiphilic interfacial microenvironment, regulating self-arrangement and suppressing disordered stacking, thereby yielding highly crystalline, continuous, and defect-free COF membranes. Moreover, the N-het-IP strategy exhibits broad universality, being compatible with various N-heterocyclic organobases and amine monomers of diverse COF membranes. Constructed via the N-het-IP strategy, the resulting COF membrane exhibits moderately high permeance and enables precise molecular sieving of dyes. The N-het-IP strategy provides a facile and efficient method to synergize the rapid synthesis and continuous assembly of COF membranes, paving the way for the development of COF membranes tailored for on-demand molecular separations.

works.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) unlock opportunities to unite rapid mass transport with molecular-level sieving through membranes. However, achieving long-range crystallographic order within these membranes remains a central challenge that limits their separation precision. Here, we report a monomer-driven strategy for the ambient-condition fabrication of COF polycrystalline membranes featuring definite lattice order and polyhedral textures, reminiscent of benchmark metal-organic framework counterparts. Using a rigid, π-conjugated pyrene-centered tetraamine, we enable nonepitaxial intergrowth of faceted COF crystals on a porous support, yielding a 350-nanometer-thick membrane with a record-high Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 2121 square meters per gram among COF separation membranes of comparable pore size. The resulting COF membrane preserves its crystallographic order and polyhedral texture even after 1 month of solvent exposure while uniquely combining increased surface stiffness with high tensile ductility. Notably, we demonstrate its superior liquid-phase molecular selectivity, outperforming COF analogs with considerably smaller pore apertures, and elucidate an unambiguous correlation between crystallographic order and permselectivity. This work positions crystallographic ordering as a guiding principle for COF membranes, opening more possibilities at the intersection of framework materials and separation technologies.

works.title: Recent Advances in the Preparation, Structural Modulation, and Applications of Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) Membrane Materials in the Field of Separation
institutions: College of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering Qiqihar University Qiqihar China
Heilongjiang Provincial Key Laboratory of Polymeric Composition College of Materials Science and Engineering Qiqihar University Qiqihar China
School of Environmental and Nature Resources Zhejiang University of Science and Technology Hangzhou China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic framework (MOF) membranes are a novel class of composite membranes. They use crystalline porous MOF materials as separation layers or functional fillers. Because of their well‐ordered and tunable pore structures and highly controllable chemical environments, MOF membranes show broad application prospects in gas separation, pervaporation, nanofiltration, ion sieving, and water treatment. This paper systematically reviews the fundamental characteristics, primary configurations, separation mechanisms, preparation methods, and structural regulation strategies of MOF membranes. It also covers their application progress in typical separation fields. First, based on the composition and structural features of MOFs, we summarize the advantages and limitations of four configurations: polycrystalline MOF membranes, mixed matrix membranes, two‐dimensional (2D) MOF layered membranes, and MOF glass membranes. The separation mechanism is then elaborated, which relies on the synergy between pore‐size sieving and chemical interactions. Second, we compare in detail the principles, applicable systems, and technical bottlenecks of various preparation methods. These include in situ growth, secondary growth, interface‐assisted growth, counter‐diffusion, vapor‐assisted conversion, and electrochemical deposition. On this basis, we systematically summarize the structural regulation strategies of MOF membranes from six aspects: crystal orientation, membrane thickness, defect engineering, intra‐pore chemical environment, interface engineering, and stability enhancement. Their influence on separation performance is also discussed. We emphasize the necessity of multi‐scale synergistic regulation. Furthermore, we present the latest research progress on MOF membranes for gas separation, pervaporation, nanofiltration, organic solvent nanofiltration, ion sieving, resource recovery, water treatment, and oil–water separation. Typical case studies are provided to analyze the structure’s performance relationship. Finally, we summarize the challenges currently faced by MOF membranes and present corresponding prospects. This paper aims to provide a systematic reference for the rational design and engineering application of MOF separation membranes.

works.title: Mathematical evaluation of forward osmosis efficiency for methylene blue removal using a flat-sheet TFC membrane
works.journal: Iraqi Journal of Chemical and Petroleum Engineering
works.abstract: Forward osmosis (FO) has gained a lot of research interest due to its many possible uses in desalination and wastewater reuse. The FO is a cost-effective method because it relies on concentration differences at the membrane surfaces and does not require external hydraulic pressure. This work deals with the design and construction of a forward osmosis system containing a membrane cell in which the thin film composite (TFC) flat sheet membrane is fixed, to carry out practical experiments by using of NaCl as the draw solution (DS), and the methylene blue (MB) dye is used as the feed solution (FS), and then employing the resulting experimental data in building and verifying the mathematical model of the FO process. The concentration of NaCl is from 5 to 70 g/L, and the concentration of MB is 20 ppm with a feeding pressure of 2 bar. A solution diffusion model was developed to predict water flux theoretically and compared with experimental results using different DS concentrations. The effect of concentration polarization was also studied. The results showed that the flux increased from 3.65 to 9.52 LMH, and the osmotic pressure at the bulk of the membrane increased linearly from 4.01 to 56.16 bar when the DS concentration increased from 5 to 70 g/L. Also, the recovery of pure water increased with increased concentration of NaCl. The results showed that there was a good agreement between the experimental and theoretical results obtained from the mathematical model, where the correlation coefficient (R2) was 98.89%.

works.title: MXenes: Types, preparation, and applications in water treatment
works.journal: Iraqi Journal of Chemical and Petroleum Engineering
works.abstract: MXenes have attracted significant attention as advanced 2D materials for water treatment, but previous assessments have been largely descriptive and have not adequately compared material types, manufacturing strategies, and practical performance. This paper aims to evaluate MXene-based membranes in terms of composition, surface chemistry, interlayer engineering and membrane design and to relate properties to water flux, rejection efficiency, adsorption capacity, antifouling behaviour and stability. Our goal is not to provide general summaries, but to highlight the critical points that will guide MXenes from laboratory demonstrations to real-world applications in water purification. This review also addresses major challenges including oxidation, restacking, swelling, mechanical fragility, scalability and environmental safety. Such a contrast between existing gaps and present advances provides a more lucid basis for the selection and design of MXene membranes in sustainable water treatment applications.

institutions: N.I. Vavilov Research Institute of Plant Industry
National Technical University of Ukraine “Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute”
works.abstract: Providing environmentally safe drinking water and treating wastewater relies heavily on efficient desalination methods. Among these, low-pressure reverse osmosis (RO) is highly promising for residential and industrial water conditioning. However, a significant operational challenge remains scaling – the deposition of mineral precipitates on the membrane surface, which reduces membrane lifespan and efficiency. The primary aim of this research is to evaluate the performance of low-pressure RO membranes, specifically the Filmtec TW30-1812-75 model, during the desalination of municipal tap water. The study focuses on assessing the intensity of sediment deposition depending on the permeate recovery rate and the influence of water acidification on mitigating these deposits. The experimental study utilized a custom-designed laboratory reverse osmosis filtration unit operating at a constant pressure of 6.1 atm with a membrane specific flux of 0.0289 m/h. Tap water, characterized by an initial total hardness of 3.8-4.9 meq/dm3 and an alkalinity of 3.7-4.3 meq/dm3, was subjected to filtration. The permeate recovery rate was systematically varied from 40% up to 90%. To investigate the anti-scaling effect of pH adjustment, the feed water was acidified using hydrochloric acid (HCl) at doses of 1.25 meq/dm3 and 2.5 meq/dm3. Key physicochemical parameters, including total hardness, calcium and magnesium concentrations, total alkalinity, electrical conductivity, and pH, were rigorously monitored in both the permeate and the concentrate. To quantify the extent of scaling on the membrane surface, a mass balance approach was employed, comparing the theoretically calculated ion concentrations in the concentrate with the analytically measured values. The findings indicate that without pre-acidification, the low-pressure RO membrane exhibits excellent desalination efficiency, reducing the permeate hardness to 0.022-0.060 meq/dm3, which corresponds to a high selectivity of 98.75-99.45%. The residual alkalinity of the permeate decreased to 0.29-0.36 meq/dm3 (selectivity 91.43-93.1%). However, mass balance calculations revealed that scaling phenomena-primarily calcium carbonate precipitation-intensify substantially when the permeate recovery rate exceeds 65%. At a 90% recovery rate, the discrepancy between the theoretical and measured hardness in the concentrate reached 28.82 meq/dm3, confirming massive sediment deposition. The introduction of hydrochloric acid effectively lowered the initial alkalinity of the feed water, aiming to suppress carbonate scaling. With an HCl dose of 1.25 meq/dm3, the selectivity for hardness ions slightly decreased to 97.76-98.77%, and scaling was only partially mitigated. Increasing the HCl dose to 2.5 meq/dm3 reduced the feed water alkalinity to approximately 1.2 meq/dm3. While this aggressive acidification significantly inhibited calcium carbonate formation at moderate recovery rates, it did not completely resolve the scaling issue at the extreme recovery rate of 90%. At this threshold, the discrepancy in hardness still reached 14.84 meq/dm3. Due to the significant decrease in bicarbonate concentration and pH, there is a low probability of hardness ion precipitation using carbonates; therefore, the precipitation of other sparingly soluble salts, such as calcium sulfate (gypsum), likely occurred due to high concentration polarization. The practical significance of this work lies in defining the operational limits for low-pressure RO systems. It was established that operating below a 65% permeate recovery rate is critical to preventing severe scaling during standard tap water desalination. Acidification proves to be a viable method for increasing the recovery threshold by lowering alkalinity; however, it has limitations at very high recovery ratios due to the shifting solubility limits of non-carbonate scaling agents. Future investigations should focus on comparing the efficacy of polyphosphate, phosphonate, and sulfonate antiscalants to further optimize the stabilization of feed water in low-pressure RO applications.
